label: Card Shuffle
blurb: The shot is a deck of cards held square in the frame, and the cut happens inside a riffle. The deck splits into two halves that lift apart and fan, the halves drop back into one another card by card, and the pack squares itself up again with the new shot on top. The faces are not just the two shots: Faces across the cut spreads the deck through the whole cut, so the card near the bottom is the old shot, the card on top is the new one, and every card between them is a step along the way, which makes the riffle read as a run of frames rather than two pictures stacked. Cards that turn over sets how many of them spin face down and back up again on the way through, showing the card back in your own colour as they pass side on. Pick a picture of your own for the card backs, and another to deal into the middle of the deck as faces (a logo, a still from between the shots, a title card). Set the size of the deck, how wide it fans, how far the cards turn, how large they sit in the frame and how heavy the shadows are between them.
